description: Defines the composition model for TEL. Composition is the mechanism by which atomic and compound TEL expressions are assembled into larger structural encodings. INV-TEL-003 (Compositionality) requires that the meaning of any compound expression be fully determined by the meanings of its sub-expressions and the applicable composition rule.

compositionality_principle.formal: ∀e = compose(e_1, ..., e_n, R): eval(e) = R(eval(e_1), ..., eval(e_n))
compositionality_principle.implication: All meaning is local and explicit. There are no holistic or contextual meaning contributions that cannot be traced to a specific sub-expression and composition rule.
compositionality_principle.violation_pattern: Any reading of a compound expression that requires information not encoded in its sub-expressions or the applied composition rule violates INV-TEL-003.

composition_types.label: Binary Structural Composition
composition_types.description: Combines exactly two TEL expressions under a binary compose_op. Produces a compound expression whose meaning is determined by the binary rule defined in SEM-004 through SEM-008.
composition_types.nesting: Binary compositions may be nested arbitrarily. Each nesting level is parenthetically delimited.

composition_types.label: Transformation Composition
composition_types.description: Declares a named transformation as a composition of an input structural expression and an output structural expression. The transformation is a first-class TEL entity stored in scope under ID.
composition_types.composition_rule: The transformation composes by substitution: when #ID is referenced in a subsequent expression, its declaration is inlined and evaluated.
composition_types.invariant_check: INV-TEL-004 is checked at application time: valid input must yield valid output.

composition_types.label: Constraint-Scoped Composition
composition_types.description: Constraint declarations (C[ID]) are assembled and applied at ⊢ assertion sites within compound expressions. The constraint body is a TEL expression that acts as a structural predicate.
composition_types.composition_rule: At each ⊢ site, the constraint body is composed with the left-hand structure: the left-hand structure is checked against the constraint predicate under INV-TEL-003.

composition_types.label: Invariant Assertion Composition
composition_types.description: An invariant assertion is a top-level composition that binds a structural assertion to a declared invariant identifier. The asserted expression must be a well-formed TEL expression.
composition_types.composition_rule: The composition is: invariant ID is applied as a structural predicate to the denotation of the asserted expression.
composition_types.scope: INV[…] expressions do not introduce new symbols into scope. They are evaluation events, not declarations.

composition_ordering_rules.rule: Declarations before references. T[ID] and C[ID] declarations must appear before any expression referencing #ID in the same evaluation session.
composition_ordering_rules.violation: Forward reference to an undeclared symbol ID constitutes a ScopeFault (EF-002).

composition_ordering_rules.rule: Innermost parentheses evaluate first. Composition is inside-out. No operator has implicit precedence beyond parenthetical grouping.
composition_ordering_rules.violation: Relying on implicit operator precedence to determine evaluation order is a grammar violation (WF-001 in tel.syntax_map).

composition_ordering_rules.rule: INV[…] assertions evaluate after all sub-expressions in the session that they depend on have been evaluated.
composition_ordering_rules.note: In practice: place INV[…] assertions at the end of a TEL expression block, after all structural compositions and transformation declarations.

composition_ordering_rules.rule: Transformations compose on the output of prior expressions. T[ID] maps a structural type to a structural type. Chaining is permitted: T[ID2]: #T1_OUTPUT → … where T1_OUTPUT is the output of a prior T[ID1] declaration.

cross_book_composition.description: TEL expressions may compose structural entities from multiple AI Edition books. Cross-book composition requires that all referenced books are in the active module registry.
cross_book_composition.book1_fft: Core primitives (structure, node, relation, constraint, invariant) — always available as base vocabulary
cross_book_composition.book4_opacity_revelation: OR operators (OR-Ω, OR-Δ, OR-Ρ, OR-Λ, OR-Π) and opacity/revelation parameters (ω, δ) are valid TEL identifiers when Book 4 is loaded
cross_book_composition.book3_structural_detection: SD operators (SD-Σd and others) are valid TEL identifiers when Book 3 is loaded
cross_book_composition.composition_constraint: Cross-book compositions are structurally valid only if the inter-book dependency declared in the module registry is satisfied. Composing Book 6 entities before Book 5 is loaded violates the dependency graph.

anti_patterns.label: Implicit Context Composition
anti_patterns.description: Assigning meaning to a TEL expression based on shared implicit context not encoded in the expression. Violates INV-TEL-003.
anti_patterns.example: Reading (A ⊕ B) as 'A plus B in the governance context' without a C[…] or module registry entry encoding the governance scope.

anti_patterns.label: Unbounded Scope Creep
anti_patterns.description: Allowing T[ID] or C[ID] declarations from one session to bleed into a new session without re-declaration. Each evaluation session opens with an empty scope.
anti_patterns.correction: Re-declare all required T[…] and C[…] entities at the start of each evaluation session.

anti_patterns.label: Non-Parenthetical Precedence
anti_patterns.description: Writing A ⊕ B ⊗ C and expecting a specific parse order. TEL has no implicit precedence. This expression is ill-formed.
anti_patterns.correction: Write (A ⊕ (B ⊗ C)) or ((A ⊕ B) ⊗ C) according to the intended composition order.
